items.text: Summary: $\Delta$-theories
$\Delta\subset\mathbf{Cat}$ given by a pair of sets of diagrams $(D',D »)$: limits of type $D'$ (inverse) and $D »$ (direct), functors commuting with them; maybe extra exactness properties.
T\colon\Delta\to\mathbf{Cat},\qquad C\mapsto T(C)\quad\text{(2-functor)}
$\Delta$-theories form a 2-category; inside it, the 2-subcategory of algebraic theories, built stepwise.
Last step: passage to the limit
T_\alpha\to T^I\ \text{algebraic (filtering)}\ \Longrightarrow\ \varprojlim_{2}T_\alpha\ \text{algebraic over } T^I
Equivalent: a 2-product of algebraic theories over $T^I$ is algebraic, with base set $I$.
Main open problem
\mathrm{Rep}\ \simeq\ \Delta^{\circ}\ \ (R\mapsto T_R)\ \supset\ \text{algebraic theories}\ \simeq\ (\text{algebraic objects of }\Delta)^{\circ}
Expected: « algebraic » objects of $\Delta$ resemble objects with a small family of generators; to be made precise.
Algebraic $R$: a discrete category $I$ and $I\to R$ with $R$ reached by a transfinite sequence $(R_\alpha)$:
R_0=\widetilde{I}^{\,\Delta}\ \ (\Delta\text{-envelope}),\qquad R_{\alpha+1}=B(R_\alpha)\ \text{or}\ C(R_\alpha),\qquad R_\alpha=\varinjlim_{\beta<\alpha}R_\beta\ (\alpha\ \text{limit})
B: make arrows invertible / equalise pairs of arrows, within $\Delta$ (adds axioms). C: add arrows (adds data).
R_\alpha=R\quad\text{for }\alpha\gg0\ (\text{in the universe})
Problem 3
Hoped: $I$ generates $R$ iff $\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(R,C)\to C^I$ is faithful. False (Isbell's example).
Problem 3: given problems 1 and 2 solved,
R \text{ is reached transfinitely from } I\ \overset{?}{\iff}\ \big(R'\subset R\ \text{full, stable under }\Delta,\ I\to R\ \text{factors through } R'\ \Rightarrow\ R'=R\big)
I_0=\langle I\rangle\subset R,\qquad I_{\alpha+1}=I_\alpha+\text{limits of type } D',D »,\qquad I_\alpha=\bigcup_{\beta<\alpha}I_\beta
The condition says exactly: this construction ends at $R$ — $I$ generates $R$ under the operations of $\Delta$.
One implication not proved; the other perhaps easy.
Smallness
When is a given $R$ algebraic? No problem if $D',D »$ are essentially small: then the algebraic $R$ are exactly the small ones (take $I=\mathrm{Ob}\,R$).
The question is real only if diagrams of arbitrarily high cardinality are allowed.
Adding arrows only finitely often
A small number of steps, each adding a small bunch of arrows.
Enlarge $I$ to contain their sources and targets: then no arrows need be added any more, only axioms.
I'=\text{full subcategory of } R \text{ on the enlarged } I,\qquad T_{I'}(C)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathbf{Cat}}(I',C)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_\Delta(I'_\Delta,C)
T_R\longrightarrow T_{I'_\Delta}\ \ \text{fully faithful}
Three steps: A discrete set $I$; C add arrows; B add axioms (composites equal).
But the axioms may produce new objects (limits, amalgamated sums), allowing new axioms: possibly still transfinite.
R_{\alpha+1}=R_\alpha[\Sigma^{-1}]:\quad T_{\alpha+1}\to T_\alpha\ \text{fully faithful, a localisation}
Intrinsic criterion for representability?
Algebraic theories (built stepwise) vs objects of $\Delta$ with a smallness condition — is there an internal property of $T$?
Ordinary categories: $F\colon C\to\mathbf{Sets}$ representable if it commutes with inverse limits (and $C$ has a small cogenerating family).
T\Big(\varprojlim_{2}C_i\Big)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\varprojlim_{2}T(C_i)
Then $T$ is pro-represented by an inverse system whose index may not lie in the universe.
u\colon C\to C'\ \text{in }\Delta\ \text{(fully) faithful}\ \Rightarrow\ T(u)\colon T(C)\to T(C')\ \text{(fully) faithful}
Evident for representable $T$ since $\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(R,-)$ preserves it.
In $\Delta$: the one-point category resembles a generator, nothing resembles a cogenerator.
Exactness properties
\Delta_D=\text{categories with limits of type } D;\quad R\in\Delta_D,\ \Sigma\subset\mathrm{Ar}(R)
C\in\Delta:\iff\ \forall F\colon R\to C \text{ in }\Delta_D,\ F(s)\ \text{invertible for } s\in\Sigma\ (\text{or equalises } \Sigma')
R\to R'\ \text{universal};\qquad C\in\Delta\iff \operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta_D}(R',C)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta_D}(R,C)
Generalised exactness properties
R\to R'\ \text{in }\Delta_D:\quad \operatorname{Hom}(R',C)\to\operatorname{Hom}(R,C)\ \text{equivalence / fully faithful / faithful}
Stability results (2-inverse limits in $\mathbf{Cat}$, etc.) survive; iteration possible, even transfinite.
Perhaps all admit solutions to problems 1 and 2.
Examples, $D=\varnothing$ (so $\Delta_D=$ all categories)
R=\{\,a\to b\,\},\ \text{require this arrow invertible}\ \Longrightarrow\ C\ \text{is a groupoid}
R=\{\,X\rightrightarrows Y\,\},\ \text{the two arrows equal}\ \Longrightarrow\ C\ \text{is preordered}
If $X\to Y\to X$ then both composites are identities: $X\cong Y$. Preordered categories $\simeq$ preordered sets, 2-equivalent to ordered sets.
Groupoids and preorders are opposite extremes; both: discrete categories $\simeq$ sets.
Problems 1 and 2 in these cases
All categories. Problem 1: $I\mapsto I$. Problem 2: category of fractions $I[\Sigma^{-1}]$ (Gabriel–Zisman).
Groupoids. Problem 1: the fundamental groupoid of a category: components = components of $I$, with fundamental groups attached.
I\mapsto I[\mathrm{Ar}(I)^{-1}]\ \ \text{is a groupoid};\qquad \text{problem 2: } C[\Sigma^{-1}]=C
Preordered. Problem 1: same objects, $X\succeq Y$ iff there is an arrow $X\to Y$.
Problem 2: pass to the ordered set (quotient by the preorder), then quotient by the relation generated by $x_i=y_i$.
Discrete categories. Problem 1:
I\mapsto \pi_0(I)\ \text{(connected components)};\qquad \text{problem 2: } C[\Sigma^{-1}]=C
Any $R\to R'$ gives such a property: $\operatorname{Hom}(R',C)\to\operatorname{Hom}(R,C)$ an equivalence. Do problems 1 and 2 have a solution?
Limits in $T(C)$
T=T_R,\qquad T(C)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_\Delta(R,C)
Existence and computation of inverse limits of type $\delta$ in $T(C)$ (dually direct limits).
